title: PasswordResetForm
wrapsNative: VStack with a switch over the steps, onSubmit, onOpenURL for the Universal Link, textContentType(.emailAddress) and the .newPassword content type of MonarchPasswordInput
summary: A recipe, not a component: request a reset link by email, then, when the emailed link opens the app, choose a new password with a live strength meter.
whenToUse: For a 'Forgot password' flow in an app that signs people in with its own email and password.
whenNotToUse: When people sign in with Rook ID, Sign in with Apple or passkeys, the provider owns password reset; link to it instead. For changing a password while signed in, ask for the current password with MonarchPasswordInput instead of a link.
api: MonarchButton("Send reset link", variant: .primary, isLoading: isWorking, fullWidth: true) { … }

states.name: request
states.description: The email field and Send reset link. An invalid address shows its error on the field.

states.name: sent
states.description: Check your email, naming the address, with a way back to use a different email.

states.name: reset
states.description: Opened by the emailed link: the new password with the strength meter and the confirmation. Change password stays disabled until every rule is met and the two match.

states.name: done
states.description: Password changed, with Back to sign in.

states.name: working
states.description: The primary button shows its spinner while the request or the save runs.

states.name: failed
states.description: A request or save that throws puts its message in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the step; an expired link is shown the same way on the reset step.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: titles in the title style, MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput with their own borders and errors, the strength meter's segments, and full-width primary buttons.
platformNotes: The web's PasswordResetForm is one component with a step prop and messages; on iOS it is a recipe, because the steps, the network calls and the link handling belong to the app. The link returns through a Universal Link (an associated domain) handled with onOpenURL, which the web gets from the page URL. The web's resend cooldown on the sent step is not part of the recipe: Monarch's cooldown logic is internal to MonarchEmailVerificationBanner today. The web moves focus to each step's heading; SwiftUI keeps VoiceOver focus where it can, so the recipe marks each title as a header and the app can post an announcement when the step changes. On a device, add keyboardType(.emailAddress) and textInputAutocapitalization(.never) to the email field; they are left out of the compiled example because the host build also targets macOS.
accessibility: Each step's title has the header trait.
The email and password fields are MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput, so labels, errors and announcements of errors come from those components.
The password inputs use the new-password content type, so iOS offers a strong password and saves it to the keychain.
The strength meter reads each rule as met or not met, not by colour alone.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets and a busy state while working.
edgeCases: Say that a link was sent whether or not an account exists, so the form does not reveal which addresses have accounts.
The reset step needs the token from the link; keep it in the app and send it with the new password.
A link opened after it expired should show the error on the reset step and offer to request a new one.
